doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mary Lou Williams's Harlem apartment
summary: Jones visited her apartment once, never knew her well, and calls her a fine pianist and composer.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think it was that Mary Luke Williams apartment when she lived in Harlem. It was either there or backstage at a theater. You cannot tell from the picture.
Is this the famous apartment where all those musicians got together?
There where a lot of musicians. But, I think it was around hundred and 47th or 48th St. It was right in there on St. Nicholas.
I didn't know her at all. I went there with a trumpet player. It wasn't Joe Wallace,… He knew very well that I did not know her. She was a very fine pianist. She wrote some great tunes.
Were even if one of those famous sessions that she had with musicians?

No. I would have remembered that. I saw somewhere on TV, late last night, where some woman in Harlem has been having sessions like that for about 10 years or so at her apartment. I think they had it on CBS… No, it wasn't on CBS. It was on Fox. She is not going to catch a cold with being barefoot like that is she? Unknown: No, I’m okay. Thank you Mr. Jones.
Okay, because I have the air-conditioning on. Maybe I should turn that off.
